speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass. To help me determine the nature of this mass and its impact on your breathing, can you tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms and if you have noticed any changes in your urination or bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Cancer with Malignant Ascites.

Given the rapid onset of shortness of breath and abdominal girth increase over one month in a 40-year-old woman with a known large ovarian mass, the clinical picture strongly suggests a malignant process causing significant ascites. I will proceed with imaging to confirm the extent of the disease.
